note: 公开文档表格结构化提炼：Log Identifier / Severity / Explanation / Action

records.explanation: Controller could not validate PMKID provided by client. This may have different triggers
records.action: Update client to latest, if issue persists, collect RA traces and over the air capture

records.explanation: Client excluded due to wrong PSK password
records.action: Check PSK configuration on client

records.explanation: Client sent invalid data rates during association request
records.action: Possible client side defect. Collect RA traces and over the air capture

records.explanation: Client sent invalid Information Element
records.action: Possible client side defect. Collect RA traces and over the air capture

records.explanation: Client requested invalid Group cipher during association
records.action: Possible client side defect. Collect RA traces and over the air capture

records.explanation: Client requested invalid Unicast cipher during association
records.action: Possible client side defect. Collect RA traces and over the air capture

records.explanation: Client requested invalid Authentication Key Management during association
records.action: Possible client side defect or configuration. Collect RA traces and over the air capture

records.explanation: Client invalid RSN version during association
records.action: Possible client side defect. Collect RA traces and over the air capture

records.explanation: Client provided invalid RSN capabilities during association
records.action: Possible client side defect. Collect RA traces and over the air capture

records.explanation: Controller received PMK with invalid length
records.action: Possible Radius server issue. Collect RA traces to confirm and check server side

records.explanation: Invalid EAPoL message received from client. malformed EAP frame
records.action: Possible client side defect, collect RA trace and over the air capture

records.explanation: Invalid EAPoL message received from client. Unexpected install bit
records.action: Possible client side defect, collect RA trace and over the air capture

records.explanation: Invalid EAPoL message received from client. Key Error bit set
records.action: Possible client side defect, collect RA trace and over the air capture

records.explanation: Invalid EAPoL message received from client. Key ACK bit set
records.action: Possible client side defect, collect RA trace and over the air capture

records.explanation: Invalid EAPoL message received from client. Invalid key type
records.action: Possible client side defect, collect RA trace and over the air capture

records.explanation: Invalid EAPoL message received from client. Unexpected secure bit set
records.action: Possible client side defect, collect RA trace and over the air capture

records.explanation: Invalid EAPoL message received from client. Key version mismatch
records.action: Possible client side defect, collect RA trace and over the air capture

records.explanation: Invalid EAPoL message received from client. Key MIC bit was not set
records.action: Possible client side defect, collect RA trace and over the air capture

records.explanation: Internal error, could not allocate data structures to handle  client for anchored WLAN
records.action: Collect RA traces,  show tech wireless, and contact Cisco Support

records.explanation: Authentication configuration is missing. Applies to 802.1x or MAB
records.action: Check authentication lists in WLAN and AAA config in policy profile

records.explanation: Controller internal error while creating client interface
records.action: Collect RA traces for further analysis

records.explanation: Client sent invalid TSPEC during roaming
records.action: Possible client defect or invalid configuration

records.explanation: During RSN Information element processing, the group key provided by client is invalid
records.action: This is probable client side issue. Check RA traces, and contact client manufacturer

records.explanation: Radius server sent an invalid PSK attribute
records.action: Check Radius server logs and configuration

records.explanation: Radius server sent an invalid PSK mode attribute
records.action: Check Radius server logs and configuration

records.explanation: AP deleted client, as it sent managemnt frame with wrong BSSID address
records.action: This is potential defect. It may need RA traces, AP logs and OTA to isolate trigger

records.explanation: AP was not able to allocate memory to handle client in WCP component. Possible defect or capacity problem
records.action: Collect AP show tech, check AP load, and possibly contact TAC for further memory analysis

records.explanation: AP deleted client as it received add request marked as WGB client for non-existing WGB entry. Possible defect
records.action: Collect RA traces, AP debug

records.explanation: Client legacy rates requested do not match association response rate. Possible defect (client side and network as it should have rejected)
records.action: Collect OTA and RA traces for client

records.explanation: Number of VHT streams requested for client is higher than 8. Possible defect
records.action: Collect OTA and RA traces, AP debugs for client

records.explanation: Invalid replay counter received during EAPoL negotiation. Client should recover on new attempt
records.action: Possible client side issue. If issue persists, collect RA traces and over the air capture

records.explanation: Client did not complete Broadcast key rotation. This may happen if client was sleeping or out of coverage
records.action: None required, as it may happen on normal scenarios. If issue persists, collect RA trace and over the air capture

records.explanation: Failure during FT processing for client. This may have different triggers
records.action: RA trace needed to isolate fault

records.explanation: Radius server was not reachable
records.action: Check WLC and Radius server logs for possible triggers. Confirm server is reachable and up

records.explanation: AP sent radio down event, leading to client delete
records.action: There are valid reasons for this to happen, if this is frequent even, check AP logs

records.explanation: Association response creation fail, possible due to client malformed request
records.action: if issue persists, collect RA traces and over the air capture

records.explanation: Default code when no other reason is known, it should have been replaced with corresponding delete trigger, internal error. Client will recover after a new session
records.action: Collect RA trace for the client

records.explanation: Default code when no other reason is known, it should have been replaced with corresponding delete trigger, related to SISF/Guest anchor component. Client will recover after a new session
records.action: Collect RA trace for the client

records.explanation: Error handling the security session of the client. Triggers could be FT roam, PMK error during iPSK, client orchestration
records.action: If this happens frequently, collect RA trace for further investigation

records.explanation: Client associated to Flex AP, and did not complete onboarding process, may be triggered if client was on low RF, or did not do local authentication
records.action: None required, if this happens frequently, collect RA and AP side debugs for the client

records.explanation: Internal error processing operation for Client in dataplane
records.action: If the issue persists, collect RA traces and contact Cisco Support

records.explanation: Client removed after inter-WNCD roaming
records.action: Validate tag and policy configuration. If this happens frequently, collect RA trace for further investigation

records.explanation: Default client exclusion reason, when something more precise was not found
records.action: If this happens frequently, collect RA trace for further investigation

records.explanation: Session was disconnected, may be triggered by radio down
records.action: None required, if this happens frequently, collect RA and AP side debugs for the client

records.explanation: Client failed SAE authentication
records.action: Check configuration and configured password

records.explanation: SAE authentication protocol error. May be triggered by client side defect, or replay attack
records.action: None required, if this happens frequently, collect RA and over the air capture for the client

records.explanation: 802.11r(FT) client sent invalid mobility domain
records.action: Possible client side defect. Collect RA traces and over the air capture

records.explanation: AP-COS in Flex mode with central association. This is not supported scenario. Not applicable to releases 17.6 and higher
records.action: Change the configuration on the policy profile.

records.explanation: if WLAN is PSK, possible invalid password. For 802.1x, this is client side supplicant issue
records.action: For PSK, check password on WLAN and client side. For 802.1x, contact client manufacturer

records.explanation: Client was deleted due to suspected mac theft, MAC was seen on different anchor or vlan in case of wired guest
records.action: Check topology, and confirm if mac movement is possible, this is spoofing, or false positive

records.explanation: Client tried to reuse IP registered to another device. High probability, it is client side issue
records.action: Check client side logs, and confirm DHCP server configuration. Update client

records.explanation: This is related to iPSK scenarios: AAA override returned password is not proper length or format, PSK is not configured properly for AAA override,
records.action: Check Radius server returned attributes

records.explanation: Client deleted during association processing, or MAB error
records.action: Check radius logs for client address. if no issues found, collect RA and over the air traces

records.explanation: Internal error, Client handling failure during guest access or anchored WLAN
records.action: Collect RA traces and contact Cisco Support

records.explanation: Internal error, Client Mobility error on anchored WLAN
records.action: Collect RA traces and contact Cisco Support

records.explanation: Internal error, could not map client to WLAN/Policy profile table (MBSSID)
records.action: Collect RA traces, show tech wireless, and contact Cisco Support

records.explanation: Internal error, controller detected congestion while creating WLAN anchor request for client
records.action: Collect RA traces,  show tech wireless, and contact Cisco Support

records.explanation: AAA reauthentication failure. This should not be applicable to  wireless clients
records.action: None required

records.explanation: Invalid EAPoL message received from client
records.action: Possible client side defect, collect RA trace and over the air capture

records.explanation: Traffic for client arrived at different interface from the currently associated one. Possible race condition
records.action: Collect RA traces,  show tech wireless, and contact Cisco Support

records.explanation: QoS policies for client could not be applied
records.action: Validate QoS config at WLAN, if no problems found, collect RA traces and contact Cisco Support

records.explanation: Internal error. Controller could not send QoS update for client to AP or mobility
records.action: Collect RA traces,  show tech wireless, and contact Cisco Support

records.explanation: Internal error. AP  could not apply QoS update for client
records.action: Collect RA traces,  show tech wireless, and contact Cisco Support

records.explanation: Internal error. AP  could not apply QoS update for client
records.action: Collect RA traces,  show tech wireless, and contact Cisco Support

records.explanation: Failure to apply authorization, possible VLAN not existing
records.action: Check VLAN in use, and attributes returned by Radius server if using AAA override

records.explanation: Failure to apply authorization, possible ACL not existing
records.action: Check ACL in use, and attributes returned by Radius server if using AAA override

records.explanation: Failure to apply authorization, possible URL redirect ACL not existing
records.action: Check URL redirect ACL in use, and attributes returned by Radius server if using AAA override

records.explanation: Client deleted during accounting of authorization process
records.action: Check RA traces for details

records.explanation: Registration of Trustsec CTS functions for client failed
records.action: Check RA traces for details

records.explanation: Client deleted as URL filter does not exist
records.action: Check WLAN/Flex profile configuration

records.explanation: Post authentication filter type received for client, is invalid
records.action: Check configuration in WLAN profile

records.explanation: For 17.3/17.6 this may indicate client did ARP flood
records.action: Check client for applications doing network scan, in some scenarios it may need client driver updates

records.explanation: Default reason for policy error, when no more detailed information is available
records.action: Check Radius server returned attributed. Collect RA traces for further analysis

records.explanation: Registration for internal reauth  for client failed
records.action: Check RA traces for details

records.explanation: Unknown failure for EPM component for client policies
records.action: Check RA traces for details

records.explanation: AAA subsystem not ready
records.action: Confirm radius server is reachable, then collect RA traces for client, and contact Cisco Support

records.explanation: Controller internal error. Client association processing was not completed in time, could be load issue
records.action: Collect RA traces for further analysis, include AP logs if Flexmode

records.explanation: Controller internal error. Client mobility processing was not completed in time, could be load issue
records.action: Collect RA traces for further analysis

records.explanation: Controller internal error. Client IP static check on mobility  was not completed in time, could be load issue
records.action: Collect RA traces for further analysis

records.explanation: Controller internal error. Client connection data creation in DB did not complete in time
records.action: Collect RA traces for further analysis

records.explanation: Internal controller error. It was not possible to find valid guest LAN and policy profile for client
records.action: Collect RA traces and contact Cisco support

records.explanation: Internal error, could not allocate data structures to handle  client for wired guest LAN
records.action: Collect RA traces,  show tech wireless, and contact Cisco Support

records.explanation: Internal error, could not send client creation event for wired guest LAN
records.action: Collect RA traces,  show tech wireless, and contact Cisco Support

records.explanation: EoGRE Tunnel join failed
records.action: Check controller and gateway configuration

records.explanation: Controller internal error while updating client interface
records.action: Collect RA traces for further analysis

records.explanation: Invalid VLAN for EoGRE client
records.action: Check configuration

records.explanation: No domain provided for EoGRE client
records.action: Check authentication logs and configuration

records.explanation: Unknown domain provided for EoGRE client
records.action: Check authentication logs and configuration

records.explanation: Tunnel for domain is shut down
records.action: Check authentication logs and configuration

records.explanation: Destination GW for EoGRE client is invalid
records.action: Check configuration

records.explanation: All destination GWs for EoGRE client are down
records.action: Check configuration

records.explanation: EoGRE Flex LS AP reported no active GW
records.action: Check AP logs and profile configuration

records.explanation: Controller internal error. Rule matching for EoGRE client failed
records.action: Collect RA traces and check with Cisco support

records.explanation: Controller internal error. Application of AAA attributes for EoGRE client failed
records.action: Collect RA traces and check with Cisco support

records.explanation: Controller internal error. Creation of  EoGRE client failed
records.action: Collect RA traces and check with Cisco support

records.explanation: Controller internal error. Mobility handling of  EoGRE client failed
records.action: Collect RA traces and check with Cisco support

records.explanation: QOS module operation failed for the client
records.action: If the issue persists, collect RA trace for further investigation

records.explanation: Used when WGB tries association to webauth WLAN
records.action: Correct WGB configuration

records.explanation: CAC TSPEC error due to insufficient bandwidth on AP radio
records.action: Check CAC configuration, and collect RA trace

records.explanation: Internal controller error. Client connection abort received during state processing
records.action: Collect RA traces for further investigation

records.explanation: Controller internal error. It was not possible to send EAPoL M1 to AP
records.action: Collect RA traces for further investigation

records.explanation: Controller internal error. It was not possible to send EAPoL M3 to AP
records.action: Collect RA traces for further investigation

records.explanation: Radius server returned a WLAN ID attribute, not matching client policy
records.action: Check if this is expected, and confirm Radius server configuration vs controller WLANs

records.explanation: Policy validation error of the supplicant name
Error handling username attribute
records.action: Collect RA traces

records.explanation: Invalid SSID name received from AAA server
records.action: Check Radius server configuration and collect RA traces for more info

records.explanation: Error handling Anchor VLAN ID attribute
records.action: Check Radius server configuration and collect RA traces for more info

records.explanation: Internal controller error while handling Accounting Interim interval settings
records.action: Collect RA traces for more info

records.explanation: Invalid Local-link bridging VLAN assigned to client
records.action: Check configuration and RA traces

records.explanation: Client removed due to mobility tunnel going down
records.action: Check mobility peer status

records.explanation: Security processing for a L3 Auth failed (Webauth/guest)
records.action: Confirm username/password and if required, collect RA trace

records.explanation: Client was deleted due to CAPWAP tunnel failure
records.action: Confirm if there are any network connectivity issues, if none found, check AP logs for any crash

records.explanation: Mac address was seen as wired WGB client, has now associated as wireless client
records.action: This is unusual scenario. Check if this is intentional

records.explanation: AP triggered delete, as client sent class 3 frame (data, power save, some management) from non-authenticated client, may happen occasionally on connection recovery
records.action: Nothing required, unless this is happening frequently. This may need RA trace and OTA capture

records.explanation: AP deleted client, as Auth request was FT or SAE, and these are not enabled in the SSID
records.action: Possible client side defect, may need OTA and config to validate

records.explanation: AP rejected association request. This could be due to invalid rates, or other incorrect information element
records.action: If this happens frequently, it may need AP side logs + OTA

records.explanation: AP deleted client during Facebook Express wifi feature, due to missing ACL
records.action: Possible configuration error. Check assigned postauth ACL

records.explanation: AP deleted client during association phase. This may  have different triggers, from internal AP process errors, normal delete on RLANs, etc
records.action: If seen frequently or observing connection problems, collect AP logs and OTA for further analysis

records.explanation: EAPoL 4WAY exchange failed at AP side, no specific trigger
records.action: Collect AP logs/client debug for further analysis

records.explanation: Association ID assigned by controller is already in use
records.action: This may need further investigation for possible defect on either controller or AP. RA traces and AP logs will be needed

records.explanation: AP received request to delete all clients in the interface. Could be due to config change, or recovery from radio event
records.action: This could be due to config request. If none was performed, check AP logs for possible radio recovery/reset that needs to be investigated

records.explanation: AP triggered delete, may be due to AP staggered upgrade in process, or client sent more than 3 continuous requests, or during some scenarios of inter-radio roaming
records.action: Some triggers are normal during operation. If this happens frequently, collect AP debug client logs

records.explanation: AP Radio driver sent a client delete, or other component sent a downstream dissasociation request
records.action: This should not be seen,  may need additional investigation to confirm if it is valid trigger. Collect RA + AP debugs

records.explanation: AP side report of different failure points on EAPoL 4way. May be triggered by wrong PSK, or possible defects on client or infrastructure side
records.action: If using PSK, check it, otherwise, collect RA trace and AP debugs, and either EPC or OTA capture.

records.explanation: AP reports EoGRE tunnel down
records.action: This is specific to EoGRE tunnel from AP. Check network connectivity and EoGRE configuration

records.explanation: Client on RLAN with Central Switching, and AP lost CAPWAP tunnel (moved to standalone)
records.action: Check AP network connectivity to controller

records.explanation: It was not possible to add RLAN client to AP dataplane, possible defect or load related issue
records.action: Get AP logs and client debugs

records.explanation: Mac address bypass failed for RLAN client. Either not authorized client, invalid config, or radius server issue
records.action: Check Radius configuration, and mac address entry in server

records.explanation: AP deleted client, as ACL name provided, was not present in AP
records.action: Check ACL configuration, collect RA traces, AP logs, AP show tech

records.explanation: AP radio driver could not configure client encryption keys. Possible defect
records.action: Collect AP debugs for client, this may need further analysis

records.explanation: AP radio driver could not configure mesh AP encryption keys. Possible defect
records.action: Collect AP debugs for mesh AP, this may need further analysis

records.explanation: AP could not add client entry to data path during association processing. Possible defect
records.action: Collect AP show tech, and debug client

records.explanation: AP could not send Auth response to client, default delete reason for auth failures. Possible defect
records.action: Collect AP show tech, OTA  and debug client

records.explanation: AP could not send Association response to client, default delete reason for association failures. Possible defect
records.action: Collect AP show tech, OTA  and debug client

records.explanation: AP could not send deauth or dissasociate to client. Possible defect
records.action: Collect AP show tech, OTA  and debug client

records.explanation: A device sent Power Saving Poll without being associated to AP. May be client side state problem
records.action: If this happens frequently, collect OTA, and client debug bundle

records.explanation: Driver could not obtain statistics for client, leading to client delete request
records.action: If this happens frequently, collect OTA, and client debug bundle

records.explanation: FT (802.11w) roaming failed for client, with AP in Flex mode. May be client side issue
records.action: If this happens frequently, collect OTA, and client debug bundle

records.explanation: AP could not add client entry to radio driver. Possible defect
records.action: Collect OTA, ap show tech, and client debug bundle

records.explanation: AP could not add client entry to radio driver. Possible defect
records.action: Collect OTA, ap show tech, and client debug bundle

records.explanation: AP radio driver could not allocate memory to handle the client add. Possible defect
records.action: Collect OTA, ap show tech, and client debug bundle

records.explanation: AP driver deleted client, as requested crypto cipher is invalid or Unknown. Possible defect
records.action: Collect OTA, ap show tech, and client debug bundle

records.explanation: AP driver reported invalid Association ID received for client. Possible defect
records.action: Collect OTA, ap show tech, controller show tech wireless, and client debug bundle

records.explanation: AP driver reported they key type sent for client is invalid type (direction, mode, etc). Possible defect
records.action: Collect OTA, ap show tech, controller show tech wireless, and client debug bundle

records.explanation: AP driver could not program the client key into radio firmware. Possible defect
records.action: Collect OTA, ap show tech, controller show tech wireless, and client debug bundle

records.explanation: AP Radio driver received association response add with invalid HT/VHT rates or legacy rates with invalid size
records.action: Collect OTA, ap show tech, controller show tech wireless, and client debug bundle

records.explanation: AP Radio driver received association response add with invalid legacy rates, or no rates at all
records.action: Collect OTA, ap show tech, controller show tech wireless, and client debug bundle

records.explanation: AP Radio driver reports that association ID set for Client is already in use. Possible defect
records.action: Collect OTA, ap show tech, controller show tech wireless, and client debug bundle

records.explanation: AP Radio driver reports that it was not possible to link the cipher type to the key when adding the client. Possible defect
records.action: Collect OTA, ap show tech, controller show tech wireless, and client debug bundle

records.explanation: AP Radio driver reports mismatch between multicast/unicast cipher when trying to set key for client. Possible defect
records.action: Collect OTA, ap show tech, controller show tech wireless, and client debug bundle

records.explanation: AP Radio driver reports mismatch invalid key length while adding  client. Possible defect
records.action: Collect OTA, ap show tech, controller show tech wireless, and client debug bundle

records.explanation: AP Radio driver reports mismatch invalid key index while adding  client. Possible defect
records.action: Collect OTA, ap show tech, controller show tech wireless, and client debug bundle

records.explanation: AP driver creation of IO control block for client failed. Possible defect
records.action: Collect OTA, ap show tech, controller show tech wireless, and client debug bundle

records.explanation: AP driver reports that IO control block for client could not be found. Possible defect
records.action: Collect OTA, ap show tech, controller show tech wireless, and client debug bundle

records.explanation: AP driver reports that radio firmware could not add client. Possible defect
records.action: Collect OTA, ap show tech, controller show tech wireless, and client debug bundle

records.explanation: Default driver client delete reason, if no other trigger was found
records.action: Collect OTA, ap show tech, controller show tech wireless, and client debug bundle

records.explanation: This can happen during normal scenarios. Client deleted due to EAPoL M1 retries. Possible client side issue, or it roamed during auth phase
records.action: If issue persists, collect RA trace and over the air capture

records.explanation: Client removed after reaching session timeout. Normal scenario
records.action: None required

records.explanation: Controller did not learn client IP address in the allowed time
records.action: Check DHCP server and client IP configuration. Validate if DHCP required is set and client is performing DHCP negotiation. If all is correct, collect RA traces and EPC

records.explanation: Triggered by configuration changes, for example WLAN or Policy profile modifications
records.action: None required

records.explanation: For PMF clients, triggered when client did not reply to SA queries and reached max retries. Could be triggered on failed roams, or client spoofing attacks
records.action: None required, as it may happen on normal scenarios. If issue persists, collect RA trace and over the air capture

records.explanation: Client was roaming during HA failure, or Association ID conflict was detected after failover
records.action: None required

records.explanation: Client roamed across WNCD instances. This is normal scenario for default tag, or roaming across tags
records.action: None required

records.explanation: Successful inter controller client roam
records.action: None required

records.explanation: Client delete, either due to roaming while on IP learning state, or due to policy configuration mismatch
records.action: Check logging details for client. In case of mismatch, correct configuration. Delete by IP learning will happen on normal scenarios

records.explanation: Default AAA disconnect reason
records.action: None required

records.explanation: Failure while sending 802.11v Transition request frame. Causes could be 11v not supported by client, or BSS transition is not enabled on the radio
records.action: Check configuration. If this happens frequently, collect RA trace

records.explanation: Not in use
records.action: None, this should not be triggered

records.explanation: Client failed pre-authentication during FT roaming
records.action: None required, if this happens frequently, collect RA and AP side debugs for the client

records.explanation: WLAN Reanchor feature is enabled, and client was not using voice/video
records.action: None required

records.explanation: Client did not reply to EAP requests in the specified retries/time
records.action: Check client supplicant/user configuration. If persistent, collect RA traces and over the air capture

records.explanation: Client did not reply to 802.1x requests in the specified retries/time
records.action: Check client supplicant/user configuration and AAA server logs. If persistent, collect RA traces and over the air capture

records.explanation: Client failed webauth, most probably wrong username or password
records.action: Check client credentials

records.explanation: Client provided wrong username or password during 802.1x authentication
records.action: Check client credentials and supplicant configuration

records.explanation: Client did not reply to 802.1x request. Not currently used
records.action: Check client supplicant configuration

records.explanation: Failure during 802.11 auth request. Not currently used
records.action: None required.

records.explanation: Client was manually excluded by administrator
records.action: Check controller configuration, if this was not intentional

records.explanation: Not in use
records.action: None required

records.explanation: 802.1x or MAB has been disabled on the client interface. This should not be applicable to  wireless clients
records.action: None required

records.explanation: AAA lost carrier failure. This should not be applicable to wireless clients
records.action: None required

records.explanation: Client did not complete L2 auth like PSK or 802.1x,  in time. Could be normal if client roamed or went out of coverage

records.explanation: Client did not complete webauth in time. Could be normal if client roamed or went out of coverage
records.action: If it is not expected, collect RA traces for further analysis, include AP logs if Flexmode

records.explanation: EoGRE tunnel was reset
records.action: Check network status

records.explanation: Unknown client deleted after HA failover
records.action: None Required

records.explanation: Client changed WLANs/SSID

records.explanation: On client reassociation or roaming, a new VLAN was assigned. This would be caused by AAA override, different policy profiles, etc

records.action: None required

records.explanation: Client deleted due to inactivity. Normal scenario
records.action: None required

records.explanation: Client deleted by AP, due to inactivity. Normal scenario
records.action: None required

records.explanation: Client did not perform roaming on 802.11v transition request and timer expired

records.explanation: WGB wired client deleted. This may be triggered by WGB client removed due to inactivity

records.explanation: WGB moved client to a different VLAN
records.action: This is for WGB VLAN feature. Check if this is intentional

records.explanation: Wrong username or password
records.action: Check client side user configuration

records.explanation: Wired Client was deleted after WGB cleanup event
records.action: Check why WGB was deleted

records.explanation: Client initiated a deauthentication or deauthentication
records.action: None required in most scenarios. This is normal activity

records.explanation: Client reported DHCP error on deauth frame
records.action: Check DHCP server, and collect RA trace

records.explanation: Client reported EAP error on deauth frame
records.action: Check AAA server, and collect RA trace and over the air capture

records.explanation: Client reported authentication error on deauth frame
records.action: Check AAA server, and collect RA trace and over the air capture

records.explanation: Client reported idle timeout on deauth frame
records.action: None required

records.explanation: Client reported webauth error on deauth frame
records.action: Check webauth configuration and certificates

records.explanation: Client reported decryption errors on deauth frame
records.action: Get RA trace and over the air captures

records.explanation: Client informed it is going in deep sleep on deauth frame
records.action: None required

records.explanation: Client informed user requested disconnection
records.action: None required

records.explanation: Client reported generic reason in deauth frame
records.action: None required

records.explanation: Client reported generic reason in deauth frame
records.action: None required

records.explanation: Client reported AP sent disconnection in deauth frame
records.action: None required

records.explanation: Client reported disconnection due to AP beacon loss. This may be triggered by low RRSI/coverage, or AP radio resets
records.action: Check AP logs for radio reset, and confirm client was not on low coverage scenario

records.explanation: Client RSSI is lower than the configured RSSI threshold
records.action: None required, as this may be intentional. Otherwise, check 802.11v and Low RSSI threshold settings.

records.explanation: AP deleted client, triggered by a channel change request
records.action: Normally, none needed, unless this is happening too frequently, more than 4 times a day per radio

records.explanation: AP reported that client did not complete adress learning process (static or DHCP)
records.action: This may happen occasionally during normal scenarios if client roamed away or was out of coverage. If this is happening frequently or not expected, get RA + AP logs

records.explanation: AP deleted client as it did not complete onboarding after requesting a roaming (reasociation)
records.action: This may happen occasionally during normal scenarios if client roamed away or was out of coverage. If this is happening frequently or not expected, get RA + AP logs

records.explanation: AP deleted client due to dissaociation frame. Normally this only is applied for PMF(11w) enabled devices
records.action: Non required, this happens during normal operation. If a large number of events are detected, get OTA to confirm source

records.explanation: Client associated to stale SSID on AP, deleted during clean up process
records.action: None required

records.explanation: DHCP required is enabled, and client never completed DHCP negotiation
records.action: May happen during normal scenarios, if client roams out of coverage during onboarding, or goes to sleep or is turned off, during onboarding. If seen on large counts per VLAN, do client debugging and check DHCP Server pool and status

records.explanation: AP deleted client as it did not reply SA query during PMF roaming (802.11w)
records.action: May happen during normal scenarios. If frequently seen for specific client, it may be needed to do OTA, RA and AP client debug

records.explanation: AP deleted client as it roamed across SSID in the same AP
records.action: None required

records.explanation: AP had a channel change, that triggered client deletion
records.action: This may happen during normal scenarios. if this is seen very frequently on same AP, it may need RF analisys or RRM tunning

records.explanation: AP driver received a delete request for the client
records.action: PENDING

records.explanation: AP radio interface has been shutdown
records.action: This may happen by admin request

records.explanation: The radio role has changed, and can be uplink/repeater
records.action: None needed

records.explanation: Slow was disabled for MFP wlan
records.action: None needed

records.explanation: MIC (for TKIP) counter protection triggered, so AP deleted all clients
records.action: None needed, if this happens frequently, check for possible client side issues

records.explanation: VLAN/ACL mapping deleted, config change
records.action: None required

records.explanation: Client deleted by maximum frame retransmissions reached. This reason should not be active
records.action: None required

records.explanation: AP triggered a deauth during webauth/dot1x/run states, this may have been requested by controller
records.action: May happen during normal scenario (for example timeout), if this is frequent or not-expected, collect RA traces for client

records.explanation: Sensor station timeout. This reason should not be active
records.action: None required

records.explanation: AP triggered client delete, by session timeout
records.action: None required, this is normal for local auth/standalone flex scenarios

records.explanation: Bad Client, this reason code should not be active
records.action: None required

records.explanation: Uplink timeout, this reason code should not be active
records.action: None required

records.explanation: Sensor AP in operation, this reason code should not be active
records.action: None required

records.explanation: Sensor AP in operation, this reason code should not be active
records.action: None required

records.explanation: AP triggered a client delete, as client did auth phase, but never completed association
records.action: May happen during normal scenario (for example timeout), if this is frequent or not-expected, collect RA traces for client

records.explanation: AP Flexgroup name was changed by administrator, leading to client delete request
records.action: None required, configuration change

records.explanation: Client sent EAP-Logoff. This may be due to normal operation (p.e. client user changed) or it may be client supplicant error, restarting auth
records.action: This is normally expected, if happening frequently or leading to problems, this may need RA trace

records.explanation: Client did not reply to EAP requests in the specified retries/time
records.action: Check client supplicant/user configuration and AP state. If persistent, collect RA traces and over the air capture

records.explanation: MIC (for TKIP) counter protection triggered, so AP deleted all clients
records.action: None needed, if this happens frequently, check for possible client side issues

records.explanation: WLC requested to AP to delete client due to roaming event
records.action: None needed

records.explanation: Client Unknown, this should not be seen/not in use
records.action: Collect RA traces for initial analysis

records.explanation: Client did not complete reauthentication in the specified timer. This may happen on normal scenarios, if client is sleeping or out of coverage
records.action: No action needed

records.explanation: Continuous idle timeout, this should not be seen/not in use
records.action: None required

records.explanation: Client deleted during RLDP (Rogue Link Detection Protocol) execution
records.action: Expected action, depending on configuration. RLDP can be disabled, if not required by security policies

records.explanation: Client deleted by Policy Enforcement Module request. This should not be see/not in use
records.action: None required

records.explanation: All Clients on RLAN port have been deleted, this could be due to port going down, or port getting admin disabled. This could happen on normal scenarios, for example, turning off a RLAN connected device or due to admin port disable configuration.
records.action: Check port config, cable, and connected device state

records.explanation: RLAN client deleted due to inactivity timeout. This can happen on normal scenarios
records.action: None needed

records.explanation: AP deleted client, as it did not complete webauth authentication in time. This may happen on normal scenarios
records.action: if this happens for clients actively trying to login, collect RA traces,  and OTA

records.explanation: AP deleted client, as it did not complete 802.1x authentication in time.
records.action: if this happens for clients actively trying to authenticate, collect RA traces,  AP debugs, and OTA

records.explanation: AP is rejecting client association, as it did not do 802.11 authentication, possible client defect
records.action: None required, or OTA is seen frequently

records.explanation: AP deleted client, as max client setting per AP is configured
records.action: None required, or check config in WLAN profile

records.explanation: AP deleted client, as max client setting per WLAN is configured
records.action: None required, or check config in WLAN profile

records.explanation: AP deleted client, as max client setting per radio is configured
records.action: None required, or check config in WLAN profile
